1ooswr1: Compare qualities with más or menos + adjective + que and tan + adjective + como. For quantities, tanto agrees: tantas tiendas como, tanto ruido como. For actions: trabajo tanto como tú. Mejor, peor, mayor, and menor usually appear without más when they are comparatives.
1xsyhx0: This apartment is less expensive than the one downtown.
193he4y: There are as many shops as in my neighborhood.
17gy9kd: El más tranquilo de los barrios is a relative superlative: it needs a comparison group. Tranquilísimo intensifies a quality without comparing. In ads, distinguish facts (price, square meters, transport) from judgments (precioso, comodísimo). Your choice should connect a fact to a need; it is not enough to say something is better.
1sh5dnw: To compare city and countryside, also think about climate and services: a rural area may be quieter but have less transport; on the coast it is usually hotter than in the mountains. Avoid presenting a personal preference as a rule for everyone.
